question: You are completing a discharge summary for a woman who underwent emergency caesarean section for fetal distress. Which of the following is the MOST critical item to include to ensure safe continuity of care by the receiving clinician?

answers.text: The name of the scrub nurse during the operation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The scrub nurse's name is an intraoperative administrative detail that does not affect the quality of post-discharge care.

answers.text: A clear list of discharge medications with dose, frequency, route, and duration

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Medication reconciliation at discharge is the highest-risk step for post-discharge adverse events; omitting dose or duration is a leading cause of medication errors and litigation in obstetrics.

answers.text: The theatre number in which the procedure was performed

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Theatre number is a logistical detail with no impact on the safety or quality of post-discharge management.
Incorrect. While pre-pregnancy weight has some clinical relevance, it is not a mandatory discharge summary element required for immediate post-operative continuity of care.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the mandatory components of an obstetric discharge summary: diagnosis, procedure, hospital course, medication list (with full details), follow-up plan, and warning signs to return for.
Correct. Complete medication details (drug, dose, route, frequency, duration) are the single most actionable component for the follow-up clinician and the safest element to prioritise.
